references.text: God's promise to Abraham of the land from the river of Egypt to the Euphrates, describing the same geographical boundaries promised in Exodus 23:31.
A detailed description of Israel's promised borders, expanding on the promise regarding the extent of the land.
Moses reminds the people of the promise of the land from the wilderness to Lebanon and to the great river Euphrates.
The promise that God will drive out the nations from the land, as also promised in Exodus 23:31.
Reiteration of the promise regarding the land's borders from the wilderness to Lebanon, from the Euphrates to the western sea.
God confirms the promise to Joshua concerning the land's borders from the wilderness to Lebanon and to the great river Euphrates.
The fulfillment of the promise that God gave Israel the land and drove out their enemies.
During Solomon's reign, the promise regarding the land's borders from the Euphrates to the border of Egypt was fulfilled.
A prophetic psalm about the king's dominion from sea to sea and from the river to the ends of the earth.
Description of Israel's extent from the sea to the river, like a vine planted by God.
Contrasting use of geographical boundaries: Exodus defines the extent of the promised land for possession, while Ezekiel defines Egypt's destructive borders.
Theological contrast: The same geographical concept (the extent of the land) is first used to promise possession and later to warn of total destruction.
Prophetic fulfillment: Ezekiel's promise to gather the people to the land illuminates and completes Exodus' original promise to give them the land.
Narrative connection: Amos describes the fulfillment of Exodus' promise to drive out the Philistines from the land.
Covenant dynamics: Ezekiel describes the consequence (scattering) for breaking the covenant terms given in Exodus.
